POKER.NAME: Poker Game
POKER.DESCRIPTION: During my college year I worked with four other developers to create an online Poker game. The project took about six weeks and used Spring Boot for the backend, React for the frontend, and Keycloak for security. This experience helped me strengthen my skills in Java and TypeScript, and taught me how to collaborate effectively: brainstorming features, creating issues, and delivering as a team.

VR.NAME: VR Marker App
VR.DESCRIPTION:
Together with my team I developed an interactive VR application that lets prospective students experience the Applied Informatics program at KdG University.

Users explore a series of linked 360° scenes from project labs and Cisco networking lessons to campus life in the cafeteria—while freely looking around in a VR headset. Interactive markers reveal extra information or allow navigation to other scenes. Audio, scene descriptions, and optional gamification elements (like quizzes) enhance the experience.

A custom admin interface makes the platform fully configurable: staff can upload new 360° assets, define markers, link scenes, add audio, and set loop points without any code changes.

This project sharpened my skills in Unity, 360° media integration, and building user-friendly configuration tools, while providing valuable experience in collaborating with a real client and working with cutting-edge VR technology.
